item.title: Hong Kong man convicted on sedition, insulting national anthem charges walks free after winning sentence appeal
item.description: A Hong Kong man convicted on charges of sedition and insulting the national anthem has won his appeal and will not have to serve the remainder of his training centre order. Chui Hoi-chun, 21, appeared at the Court of Appeal on Thursday, more than two years after being released on bail while awaiting his appeal […]

item.title: Hong Kong gov’t hits out at Amnesty International report on ‘inhumane treatment’ in local prisons
item.description: Hong Kong authorities have condemned a recent report by Amnesty International accusing local prisons of being “rife with violence and inhumane treatment.” The Amnesty report, released on Wednesday, was described by the Correctional Services Department (CSD) as “fact-twisting” and intended to “smear” legitimate custodial management. In a statement issued on Thursday evening, the CSD criticised […]

item.title: TikTok signs joint venture deal to avert US ban threat
item.description: TikTok said Thursday it has signed a joint venture deal with investors that would allow the company to maintain operations in the United States and avoid a ban threat over its Chinese ownership. item.title: In Pictures: Hong Kong holds full-honours funeral for firefighter who died in Tai Po blaze
item.description: Hong Kong’s Fire Services Department held a funeral with full honours on Friday for firefighter Ho Wai-ho, who died in the line of duty in a blaze at Wang Fuk Court last month. item.title: Mainland Chinese man arrested for alleged 1 billion yen robbery in Sheung Wan
item.description: A mainland Chinese man has been arrested in connection with a daylight robbery involving one billion yen (HK$50 million) in Sheung Wan. item.description: The Hong Kong government has applied to dissolve the management committee of the owners’ corporation of Wang Fuk Court after a deadly fire killed at least 160 people at the housing estate in Tai Po. item.title: HKFP Lens: Crowds flock to see Kam Tin’s once-in-a-decade Jiao Festival
item.description: The once-in-a-decade Jiao Festival in Kam Tin – which features a massive centrepiece that entered the Guinness World Records as the world’s largest temporary bamboo altar – has drawn to a successful close. item.title: Taiwan lodges WTO complaint over Canadian steel tariffs
item.description: Taiwan has launched a complaint with the World Trade Organization over Canadian tariffs slapped on imports of steel goods, the global trade body said Thursday. item.title: After deadly Tai Po fire, Hong Kong’s urban redevelopment body has no room for complacency
item.description: The deadly Wang Fuk Court fire has put a spotlight on the maintenance of ageing buildings in Hong Kong.
